policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV continues the plural subject of the surrounding chain — "they laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them" — matching the qere 3mp וישתחוו rather than the ketiv 3ms, which would require "he worshipped".
ASV's main text reads "and Tamar in the wilderness", with a mapped note giving Tadmor as another reading; the text therefore follows the ketiv תמר rather than the qere תדמר.
